themes.consensus_view: Banks overwhelmingly agree that the roughly $750 billion hyperscalers will spend on AI in 2026 is the main engine behind current earnings and stock-market gains, while a vocal minority warns the rally now looks bubble-like and increasingly reliant on debt financing.

facts_agreed.claim: Hyperscaler AI capex is surging to roughly $750 billion in 2026, up about 80% year over year.
evidence_quotes: AI-related capex is surging, with the five hyperscalers forecast to invest about USD 750bn
consensus of analysts is now for the mega-cap US hyperscalers to spend $755 billion

facts_agreed.claim: AI-driven investment is a primary driver of US growth, corporate earnings, and equity-market momentum.
evidence_quotes: These include: supportive fiscal policy, AI-driven investment, and easier financial conditions.
The AI buildout has so far outweighed the typical effect of a macro shock
main drivers of our GDP forecast are the continued capital expenditures
reflects a combination of recovering advertising demand, AI-driven investment
continued business investment in AI could help sustain the recent strength
AI capital spending is not highly sensitive to gasoline or diesel prices.

facts_agreed.claim: Demand for AI chips and compute remains robust and supply-constrained.
evidence_quotes: We see robust demand for advanced chips and high-performance computing
AI-driven demand remains strong and supply-constrained
As long as the demand for top-end AI chips remains robust, Taiwan's trade prospects remain bright.
The bottlenecks are capturing extraordinary economics and capital is flooding in accordingly.
The AI memory trade continues to dominate the tape

facts_agreed.claim: The AI investment boom is driving a structural shift in S&P 500 spending away from buybacks toward capex.
evidence_quotes: The AI investment boom will drive a continued shift from buybacks to capex

facts_contested.claim: whether the AI spending boom and rally are sustainable or a bubble
facts_contested.for_evidence: The AI investment cycle still appears to be at an early stage.
banks_against: Nomura / Barclays / AXA IM / BNP Paribas
facts_contested.against_evidence: AI-led momentum shows increasingly bubble-like characteristics

themes.consensus_view: Most banks think the market has the rate-cut path wrong, but they split on which way: Citi and UBS say traders are underpricing cuts that are still coming, while Deutsche Bank, ING, TS Lombard and Barclays say sticky 3%-ish inflation means cuts come slower or not at all (and the Bank of England may even hike).

facts_agreed.claim: The skeptical camp agrees inflation is sticky enough that central banks have less room to ease than markets assume.
evidence_quotes: Rates could fall slower than growing optimism suggests
Bank of England potentially having less room to ease over the coming years.
Longer run – better growth, inflation > 3%, and Fed hikes in 2027
Fed cut expectations have been pared back, with Barclays economists now expecting only one cut

facts_agreed.claim: Bond markets are pricing in more Bank of England rate hikes than the BoE actually intends to deliver.
evidence_quotes: markets are getting ahead of themselves by pricing in rate hikes
Bank of England potentially having less room to ease over the coming years.

facts_contested.claim: whether the Fed actually cuts (markets overpricing the no-cut risk vs. cuts being repriced away)
facts_contested.for_evidence: markets continue to overprice the risk that the Fed will not cut interest rates
facts_contested.against_evidence: Fed cut expectations have been pared back, with Barclays economists now expecting only one cut
